newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors indict 10 in Hanbo crisis.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors indict 10 in Hanbo crisis.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday indicted 10 people over the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co in a loans scandal that has rocked the government of President Kim Young-sam.
Nine of those indicted, including three close aides to Kim, are already in detention in connection with the scandal. The 10th is serving jail time in an unrelated case.
Prosecutors said their probe into what is probably the biggest corporate collapse in South Korean history was now at the half-way stage.

Those indicted in Kim's inner circle include former home affairs minister Kim Woo-suk, who resigned last Wednesday shortly before being held on charges of accepting bribes from Hanbo, which folded under five trillion won ($5.8 billion) of debt.
The other two are lawmakers Hong In-gil and Hwang Byung-tai, key members of a faction that backed Kim Young-sam's rise to power.
Another member of parliament, Chung Jae-chull, the highest-ranking official in the ruling New Korea Party after the president and party chairman, was also indicted.

Three bankers have been indicted, including two former presidents of Korea First Bank, Hanbo's major creditor. One former Korea First president, Rhee Chul-soo, is currently serving a three-year jail sentence after being convicted of bribery in a separate case. The other is Sheen Kwang-shik.
The third banker is Woo Chan-mok, head of Cho Hung Bank.
Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, who was arrested on charges of fraud and violating laws on issuing cheques and trust and savings companies, was indicted along with Hanbo treasurer Kim Jong-kook.
Kwon Roh-kap, a top aide to opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, was also indicted.
